mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real interest rates, reducing present value of future corporate cash flows and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers market expectations of prolonged restrictive policy, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month) and a decline in real retail sales (implied by RSAFS < previous month) signals a divergence between income and spending, suggesting future consumption weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.2%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for six consecutive months, combined with a decline in average hourly earnings growth (implied by UNRATE and PAYEMS dynamics), signals a softening labor market that reduces wage inflation and corporate margins, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4% for six consecutive months AND PAYEMS growth < 0.2% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between real GDP growth (GDPC1 quarter-over-quarter) and S&P 500 20-day forward returns exists in expansionary regimes, such that a quarterly GDPC1 rise above 2% predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In at least 70% of quarters with GDPC1 > 2%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (> 0.4%).
